features.notes: ADDED MID-SPRINT after investigating 1.1.70's Open Question 1 BEFORE building its mitigations. The check paid for itself: AGENT_ENGINE_ID is set in dev+prod so sessions really do persist in Vertex, and the group pointer is first-wins with a 30-day TTL, so a normal rejoin resumes. Nothing was expiring. The real cause is that reset_teaching_data clears nine collections and NEITHER progress store is among them - so a dev reset wiped the conversation and the group-session pointer and left the ticks ORPHANED. Aswin rejoined, got a fresh session (pointer gone), and the tutor found four marks from a conversation that no longer existed. checklist_progress is mine from last week; concept_progress (CONCEPT-1) had the same gap and predates me - every per-group store we have added was invisible to the reset. M's call: [Reset session] clears progress too ('reset means start over'). CONSEQUENCE FOR THE SPRINT: M3/M4 drop from the floor to the cut line - they now cover only the LEGITIMATE divergences (teacher reset, TTL expiry), not the reported bug. Backend 2801 passed (+5). Lint clean.

features.description: Per-turn fill-state block over mcp_app_context, registry-driven. Server-side synthesis of EMPTY for authored-but-untouched elements so 'unknown' and 'empty' stop collapsing.
acceptance_criteria: An authored, untouched table reports EMPTY in turn one's context
An absent element reports nothing — unknown and empty never conflated
Partial reports correct counts
It is a per-TURN instruction provider, not a build-time string (fill-state changes mid-session)
Composed-prompt budget test EXTENDED FIRST, before the block is written
Registry-completeness: every element kind has a fill reader where it has a describer
features.notes: Budget test written FIRST, as the plan required, and it EARNED ITS KEEP: the first full composition came to 13,175 chars against the 13,000 ceiling even though every individual block was inside its own cap. Cause was real duplication - the checklist and checkpoint blocks each carried a near-identical contract paragraph (~450 chars of the same instruction twice, for the model to reconcile). Merged into one shared contract in adk/progress_context.py; now 12,213 + contract. The budget test now asserts against a DECLARED, commented constant (_PER_TURN_ACTIVITY_BUDGET) rather than an arbitrary number, so raising it is a visible decision. DOC PREMISE CORRECTED - 1.1.69 Open Question 2 guessed 'almost certainly' that solution + document have the same gap. They do NOT: a solution is submitted as a multimodal chat TURN (SolutionElementMount -> onProactiveTrigger) and an uploaded document rides the artifact loader/injector, so the tutor sees both in the conversation and neither writes mcp_app_context. Synthesising EMPTY for them would be FALSE the moment a student submits - the unknown/empty conflation inverted. They get an explicit NoFillChannel(reason=...) instead. Checklist likewise excluded: its authority is the Firestore store, and a third client-mirrored view would contradict it after the first AI tick. Registry test asserts every kind carries a POSITIVE decision (reader or documented exclusion) - note the default here is SILENCE, the opposite of the manifest's generic line, because a fabricated EMPTY is worse than saying nothing.

features.description: mark_checklist_item refuses when the step's associated element is demonstrably empty. Closes the loop where the tool's own instruction ('do not tick just because the student says done') was unfollowable.
acceptance_criteria: 'Done' on an empty table produces NO mark
A mark still succeeds when the element has data
Refusal carries a correctable reason the model can act on
Step-element association inferred from the step label; explicit elementId deferred
FAILS OPEN: no confident association -> allow the mark (a false refusal is worse than the status quo)
features.notes: Reads session state via ADK's tool_context injection (the adk/tools.py:46 precedent), so group_id and activity_id stay out of the model-settable surface - the existing security test was tightened rather than loosened to prove it. Association is label-based, option (a): the step names the element, OR the step names the KIND and the activity has exactly one of that kind ('Udfyld tabellen'). The calculator gets NO kind-noun rule on purpose - 'beregn' is the ordinary Danish verb for 'calculate', so 'Beregn gennemsnittet' is a TASK, and matching it would refuse marks for work done on paper. Fails open everywhere else, and never blocks UN-marking: a tutor correcting its own premature tick must always be able to. Refusals log (Axiom 8) - a counterfactual is otherwise invisible.

features.description: Wire checklist_state_summary AND checkpoint_state_summary — both currently dead code — with provenance and a continue-from-first-outstanding contract.
acceptance_criteria: A fresh session with prior ticks contains an inherited-progress block
The tutor does not claim to have witnessed inherited work

It may revisit a marked step if the student seems unsure
A test FAILS if either summary is defined-but-unwired
No progress -> empty string -> composes exactly as today
features.notes: DOC PREMISE CORRECTED, and it was load-bearing. 1.1.70's draft wording was 'progress from an EARLIER session, which you did not witness', on the premise that the block is composed once at agent build. It is not: create_agent_with_thinking is called from skills.skill_processor.process_skill_request on EVERY REQUEST, so agent-build time IS per-turn. That wording would have been a falsehood from turn two onward - about marks the tutor made itself, which it can see in its own conversation. The block now states what the store actually knows (who marked it, when, with what evidence) and asks the model to compare against the conversation it is in. Every behaviour the doc wanted survives: the record is not a memory, continue from the first OUTSTANDING step, do not re-test, a mark is not a verdict. A test pins the difference so the stronger claim cannot be reinstated without re-reading why. The unwired-guard asserts BOTH links: every adk *_state_summary is called by the designated composer, and the composer is called by the factory.

features.notes: SEED REQUIRED (make seed ENV=<env>, all three envs) - four SKILL.md openingTemplates changed. 1.1.72's Open Question 1 ('do the templates need re-authoring?') is ANSWERED YES, and not for the reason the doc expected. THREE of the four hardcoded the language ('Greet them briefly in Danish', 'Hils kort paa dansk'). The opening block is APPENDED AFTER the body that carries the 1.1.63 M2 language directive, and this codebase's convention is that later instruction wins - so those templates silently overrode the teacher's English setting on the ONE turn with no student message to infer from. The M5 acceptance criterion 'an English activity opens in English' would have failed with the Python change alone. Templates now defer to the directive, and a parametrised guard test fails on any future 'in Danish' / 'paa dansk'. concept-dialogue also carried Aswin's reported sentence nearly verbatim ('ask what concept they would like to explore') - now conditioned on no activity being described.

features.description: Read-aloud voice resolves from activity.language, not the class persona alone.
acceptance_criteria: An English activity under a Danish persona reads with an English voice
Numbers are pronounced in the activity's language
Pronunciation rule set follows the same resolved language
Persona voice still wins when the languages agree
features.notes: SCOPE CORRECTION: planned as frontend-only, is actually mostly BACKEND. The resolution lives in protocols/voice_routes.py::resolve_voice, the documented single source of truth for BOTH /config (what the frontend asks for, and where the pronunciation ruleset's lang comes from) and /synthesize (which re-resolves server-side). A frontend-only fix would have left those two disagreeing - exactly the drift ResolvedVoice was created to prevent. TWO further findings. (1) PRE-EXISTING BUG, now fixed: resolve_voice called resolve_active_config(SKILL_id), but ALS-1 M0 made the activity a distinct act- id - so the activity's PERSONA has silently not reached the voice since the re-key, and the language fix would have been dead on arrival. activity_id is now threaded through /config, /synthesize, useVoiceConfig (incl. its cache key) and the chat page. (2) The swap must be PROVIDER-AWARE: all five shipped personas are gcp_gemini with BARE voice names (Puck, Aoede) for which GcpTTS treats the caller's lang as authoritative. Substituting an en-US-Wavenet-* there would have dropped every persona from Gemini-TTS to WaveNet and discarded their voicePrompt Style Instructions, which non-Gemini tiers reject. Multilingual voices are RETUNED (lang only); only locale-bound names (da-DK-Wavenet-A, which Cloud TTS 400s on a lang mismatch) are swapped. Activity language wins only when EXPLICITLY non-default, from the same DEFAULT_ACTIVITY_LANGUAGE constant the text directive uses, so the two cannot drift.
